newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian teachers stage two-day work stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Colombian teachers stage two-day work stoppage.

text.p: School teachers across Colombia began a two-day work stoppage on Wednesday to press for wage hikes above what they have been promised for next year and enhanced social security benefits.

The strike by the 200,000-strong Colombian Federation of Educators (Fecode) shut down public schools serving about seven million students nationwide, authorities said, adding that there was no immediate news of any strike-related violence despite protest marches held in various parts of the country.

Fecode president Boris Montes de Oca said teachers' demands included calls for a wage hike above the 13 percent the government has already offered for next year, since inflation in 1996 is widely expected to reach about 21 percent.
Montes de Oca told Reuters the union was also pressing for expanded benefits under Colombia's social security system, including better health care.
He added that teachers would call an indefinite strike in October unless their demands are addressed by the government.
